spec_match.rationale: Shows the real namespaceURI/prefix/localName the parser assigns per Namespaces in XML, plus a live prefix-independent getElementsByTagNameNS query — resolution the Rust engine must reproduce exactly.

interactive.rationale: Editable source with parse-on-input, resolved-elements table, and a two-field namespace query with its own result readout.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card's promise matches the verified page behaviour.

edge_cases.rationale: Not-well-formed input collapses the table to the parsererror line and blocks queries with an instruction; query exceptions render as text; default-namespace elements show '(default)' prefix.

references.rationale: Links the ChromeStatus entry plus the exact XML spec sections the page demonstrates.

conformance.rationale: The new v153 feature suite (extending the v151 one with XHR-responseXML and SVG-as-image scenario checks) ran 7 pass / 0 fail / 0 blocked in the verification browser.

runtime_evidence.rationale: CDP page-driver run (headless Chromium 141): sample parsed 6 elements / 6 namespaced; the SVG circle query matched 1 element prefix-independently, and a second query against the dc: namespace matched the dc:title element; console/network clean; screenshot v153-xml-ns.png read.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts xml-ns-parsed with element/namespaced counts (false on parse failure) and xml-ns-query with the match count.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables only; status chips put ivory text on the emerald/rose accents (both >4.4:1); tables and code blocks scroll in their own containers.

accessibility.rationale: Status chip role=status; the table has an aria-label and column headers; query inputs are labelled; the query result is aria-live=polite.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: deno task responsive-check v153/xml-parsing-in-rust-for-non-xslt-scenarios --no-server: desktop OK clean, mobile OK (sub-44px flags are inline links; textareas, selects, and buttons remain usable); both screenshots read and judged clean.

openQuestions.title: Re-run these contract demos with the Rust parser active
openQuestions.detail: The verification browser runs the current default engine. Launch with --enable-blink-features=XMLRustForNonXslt (or a Chrome 153 build after the flip) and confirm every preset — including parsererror text, entity expansion, and namespace resolution — behaves identically, which is the feature's whole compatibility promise. Any observable difference would be a Chromium bug worth filing.

guidanceConsulted.query: xml text editor textarea live parse output accessible status
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Pair visual pass/fail chips with textual status in a polite live region, and label textareas and result regions.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Query result region is aria-live=polite; table semantics carry the resolution data.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: Driver run: both queries announced their match counts as text

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive data table small screens horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Let two-pane editors stack on narrow viewports and keep tables/code scrolling in their own container.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Controls flex-wrap; the table uses word-break to avoid overflow at 360px.

summary: v153 refile of the namespaces explorer (framing carried by the corrected feature index). Verified via CDP headless Chromium 141: real resolution table and two distinct prefix-independent queries, clean console/network.
